record.title: Iran Iraqi Kurdistan post-referendum border suspension
record.scope: Three official Iran–Iraqi Kurdistan crossings with distinct reopening phases.
record.crossings: Parwezkhan and Haji Omaran, reopened January 2 2018; Bashmakh, reopened October 25 2017.
record.exceptions: People already waiting were initially allowed through; semi-official Tawqela remained open.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no current-status inference
record.official_rationale: Response to Kurdish independence referendum and request by Iraqi federal government.
record.context: Closures accompanied measures to isolate the Kurdish region after its September 2017 referendum.
record.uncertainty: The main closure is dated October 15 by contemporary customs reporting; Iran initially denied new measures. Two gates reopened January 2 and Bashmakh October 25. Earlier drill and air measures are separate. Other reports' differing post counts remain a reporting disagreement.

historical.duration_note: 63–93 calendar days to the stated endpoint from reported date precision; not proof of continuous full closure

Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Iran's closure at Baghdad's request responded to the Kurdish independence referendum; this classification makes no sovereignty determination. Other rationale codes retain their existing evidence qualifications.
Anadolu names three terminals; baseline conservatively isolates Parwezkhan/Haji Omaran and preserves differing post counts.
Customs official describes two-and-a-half-month closure; exact day continuity remains unproven and no interval computed.
